title: The American Revolution - OverSimplified (Part 1)
beats: Columbus rants at the monarchs about reaching the wrong continent
Anticipates 'Vikings discovered America' objection, then sponsor
French and English claim same land; Washington sparks the Seven Years' War
Britain tells colonies it spent money protecting them and now needs payment
Stamp Act shown as a shopkeeper scene with stamping each step
Colonists react: boycotts hurt British business
Britain repeals, then taxes again; same boycott cycle (4:53)
Boston Massacre told as escalation: snowballs to rocks to oyster shells
Tea Party; punishments; colonies form Continental Congress
Roll call of delegates with nicknames
Lexington and Concord; militias surround Boston
Fort Ticonderoga raid and Arnold gag
Bunker Hill: technical defeat but costly for British
King's angry letter handwriting gag, colonists still unsure why they fight
Callback to 'remember all those guns?'; guns hauled and set on Dorchester Heights
Common Sense pamphlet and Declaration vote
Battle of Brooklyn: defeat, fog saves army, retreat through New Jersey

metrics.misconception: yes: Columbus did not discover America; Vikings gag at 0:47
metrics.examples: Tax cycle twice (Sugar/Stamp, Townshend), then battles of increasing scale
metrics.ending: Washington's army beaten but alive, music, part 2 implied

new_moves.name: plant-and-pay-off
new_moves.what: Mention an object (guns at Ticonderoga) then call back to it minutes later

new_moves.name: escalation-ladder
new_moves.what: Show event growth by listing steps (snowballs, rocks, oyster shells)

theory: The Stamp Act scene (3:16) turns an abstract policy into a concrete transaction the viewer can run in their head, and the tax-boycott-retreat loop teaches causation by repetition. A planted object paid off later (guns) builds memory with no notation.
velocity: Scene builder: perform a rule as a literal transaction with a visible step each time
Orchestrator: plant objects early, call back by name later (learner-model recall check)
Ghost hands: show repeated cycles twice before naming the pattern
quote: There's a whole another freaking continent out there!
